requirement_text: Common Points Scale -- Leaving Certificate Higher Level grades: H1=100, H2=88, H3=77, H4=66, H5=56, H6=46, H7=37, H8=0 points. Ordinary Level grades: O1=56, O2=46, O3=37, O4=28, O5=20, O6=12, O7=0, O8=0 points.
source_authority_note: cao.ie / www2.cao.ie is Ireland's official Central Applications Office for undergraduate admissions, established and jointly operated by the Irish higher education institutions; the domain is cao.ie, not .gov.ie, so it does not pass the narrow .edu/.ac./.gov authority gate despite functioning as the de facto official national admissions-processing system. Some documents hosted on www2.cao.ie (e.g. the 'Agreed Entry Requirements for EU/EFTA/UK' guide) are jointly authored by the participating HEIs, not by CAO itself.

requirement_text: "25 bonus points are awarded to students attaining a minimum of grade 6 in Higher Level Mathematics (H6)." For EU/EFTA/UK applicants presenting other systems: "if a candidate presents either grade H6 or better in Leaving Cert Mathematics or grade E or better in A level Mathematics, 25 bonus points will be added to the score from their school examination, provided Mathematics is one of the subjects used to attain that score." Maximum available score with bonus is 625 points.

requirement_text: General Leaving Certificate matriculation requirement for Level 8 (Honours Degree) programmes is either: "2 H5 required i.e., 6 subjects at ordinary level grade 6 or better including 2 with minimum of grade 5 at higher level" or "3 H5 required i.e., 6 subjects at ordinary level grade 6 or better including 3 with minimum of grade 5 at higher level" (varies by institution/programme). For Level 7/6 awards, matriculation is normally "5 subjects at ordinary level grade 5 or better." "In all cases English must normally be included as one of the recognised subjects."

requirement_text: CAO points are a competitive OUTCOME, not a published minimum: "A points scoring system is in operation. It is not possible to forecast how many points will be required for a particular course until the current year's examination results are known and places are allocated (mid-late August each year)." Ranking mechanism: "Eligible applicants are ranked in descending points order and places allocated from the highest score downwards until the programme is full."
